contests.title: PayPal AI Hackathon
contests.description: About the challenge PayPal already moves money for millions of people and businesses, every day, all over the world. This hackathon is us opening that platform up and asking what happens when you put AI behind the wheel. New agents, new ways to pay and get paid, tools nobody's built yet. We want to see what you make of it. AI is changing how people build, buy, sell, work, connect, and move money. Now it's your turn to imagine what comes next. Build What's Next with PayPal and AI is a global online hackathon inviting developers, designers, founders, students, and builders to create something new using PayPal and AI. There are no prescribed problem statements and no set of tracks. Build an agent, an app, an automation, a new payment experience, a business tool, a social product, or something we haven't thought of yet. The only fundamental requirement: your project must meaningfully use both PayPal and AI. Why Join? Build something ambitious — Turn an idea into a working project using PayPal and AI. Explore what’s next — Experiment with new ways people, businesses, and AI agents can interact with money and payments. Win part of $69,750 in total prizes — Compete for overall prizes and special awards across creativity, impact, execution, and more. Show what you can build — Put your project in front of PayPal judges, developers, and the wider hackathon community. Learn by building — Explore PayPal APIs, AI tools, agents, automations, and emerging development workflows. Build your way — Join individually or as a team, and start something new or meaningfully advance an existing project. Get started Get a PayPal Developer account (5 minutes) Review example projects and brainstorm your own (30 minutes) Webinars Oct 6th 9am PT - 9:45am PT ~ Start building with PayPal Recording Oct 7th 9am PT - 9:30am PT ~ Power Your PayPal Hackathon Project with APIMatic Context Plugins Oct 12th 7am PT - 7:45am PT ~ Build a payments dashboard without building a dashboard Oct 13th 1am PT - 2am PT ~ Start building with PayPal

contests.title: Kiroween 2026
contests.description: 🎃 Kiroween 2026 is open for hacking👻 Kiro’s annual Halloween-themed hackathon has returned, and building starts now. Last year, thousands of developers used Kiro to bring dead tech back to life, stitch together unexpected technologies, and create hauntingly good experiences. This year, it’s your turn. Show us how you use Kiro to push boundaries. Work across a crew of agents in Kiro Crew, add structure with specs, customize workflows with hooks or steering, streamline with Kiro powers, or bring in new capabilities with MCP. Pick a category, build something wicked, and compete for $100,000 in prizes. You have until Friday, December 4, 2026 at 2:00 PM Pacific Time to submit. Only new projects are eligible. You must build your project during the Submission Period (October 30 to December 4, 2026). Projects you started before October 30, including Kiroween 2025 projects, are not eligible. Get started Read the Official Rules. Review them before you start to build. Get free Kiro credits. Request 4,000 free Kiro credits on the Resources tab by December 1 at 12:00 pm PT. Find details on the Resources tab. Join the Kiro Discord. Get help from the Kiro team, Kiro ambassadors, and other participants in #kiroween-hackathon. You’ll also find biweekly office hours and other live events to help you along the way. Find your teammates. Browse the Participants tab (optional). Teams can have up to three members. Join the Devpost Build Session on November 11 at 10:00 AM PT. Sign up here. Start your submission early. Click “Enter a Submission” and save drafts as often as you like.

contests.description: THE META VR START DEVELOPER COMPETITION IS BACK! This year’s eight-week challenge calls on Start program members to build the next generation of Entertainment, Gaming, and Productivity experiences for Meta VR devices – including Meta VR Glasses and Meta Quest. We’re looking for hands-first apps that make interaction more natural and gameplay more intuitive than ever before. Last year, over 2,900 developers joined the competition and delivered more than 650 submissions that pushed the boundaries of immersive technology. This year, we’re raising the bar again. Whether you’re a first-time Start developer with a breakthrough idea or a seasoned creator ready to showcase what’s possible with the latest platform capabilities, this is your moment to help redefine the future of VR. Here’s what’s waiting for you: 🤝 Build hands-first. Design experiences powered by hand interactions that feel natural, responsive, and deeply immersive—no controllers required. 🛠️ Explore new tech. Take advantage of the latest OS capabilities and device features across Meta VR Glasses and Meta Quest, accelerate your development with AI tooling, including Meta VR CLI. 🌍 Join a global community. Boost your skills through mentor programming, collaborate with fellow developers, share insights, and learn from a thriving network of experienced VR developers. 🏆 Compete for $1M in cash prizes with top prizes of $100,000. The future of VR is in your hands literally. We can’t wait to see what you build. GETTING STARTED If you’re not already a member of the Start program, apply now to join the competition. contests.title: Codegeist 2026: Build with context. Ship with confidence.
contests.description: What is Codegeist? Codegeist is Atlassian’s annual hackathon where developers from around the world unleash creativity on Forge, Atlassian’s serverless app development platform. By extending Atlassian products with custom apps and integrations, participants reimagine how teams plan, track, and deliver work. The Challenge AI can think. But knowing what to do – really knowing – takes context. Atlassian’s Teamwork Graph connects goals, work, people, decisions, and outcomes like associative memory for your organization, giving teams the shared understanding of who’s doing what, what’s already been decided, and what needs to happen next. That's the problem Atlassian is built to solve. And it's the problem we're inviting you to tackle. Build an app on Atlassian’s Forge platform that uses that context to help teams ship with confidence – whether that’s surfacing the right knowledge at the right moment, connecting work across silos, or turning organizational data into a decision that actually moves work forward. Join the live Build Session Tue, Nov 17, 12:00 to 12:45 PM ET on Zoom. Danny Thompson, Senior Developer Advocate at Atlassian, and Adam Moore, Group Product Manager, Forge, show how to build AI workflows with Atlassian Forge and Rovo, followed by live Q&A. Set up Forge first and you can build along. The recording will be on YouTube afterward. Register for the Build Session

contests.title: UGREEN Hackathon 2026 on AI NAS
contests.description: UGREEN is opening AI NAS to developers through UGOS and Skills Hub. Powered by UGOS, UGREEN's own Linux-based operating system, UGREEN AI NAS brings local storage, computing, and AI capabilities together in one platform. UGOS makes it easy to keep your data secure, find and organize your files, and get more done with AI.With the UGOS Skill Creation Tool and your preferred AI assistant, you can create custom Skills that use supported NAS capabilities to organize files, find information, and automate everyday tasks. UGREEN Skills Hub gives developers the freedom to explore new ideas, create innovative tools, and expand what AI NAS can do. You bring the ideas. We'll help you build them. Access developer resources and technical support, with opportunities to win prizes, gain exposure through UGREEN, and explore future collaborations. No UGREEN NAS is required to enter. Finalists will receive free access to a UGREEN AI NAS iDX6011 Pro environment for final development, testing, and validation. The Hackathon has two rounds: Round 1 (open to all): Share your idea and an early build of your Skill. You do not need a NAS to enter. Download the UGREEN Skill Developer Package. Then submit a short PDF and a Pre-test Skill Package (ZIP). Round 2 (Finalists only): UGREEN will select up to 30 Finalists. Each Finalist gets one assigned testing day of free remote access to a real UGREEN AI NAS to install, test, and polish their Skill. Finalists then submit their final Skill and a short demo video to compete for $46,000 in cash prizes! Get Started: 🧠 Get to know UGREEN AI NAS. Learn what it can do. 💬 Join the UGREEN Community. It's a place to find teammates, compare approaches, and get help when you're stuck, while keeping up with official Hackathon news and development resources and discovering community perks. ✨ 📦 Download the UGREEN Skill Developer Package. It has the tools and technical docs you need. You must use this package to build your Skill. 🛠️ Brush up on helpful skills. Python or JavaScript/TypeScript, Linux and Docker, AI agent and tool design, and file or media processing are all useful here. Why Participate 💰 Compete for $46,000 in cash prizes. Five winners will share the prize pool, including two Most Creative awards. 🚀 No NAS needed to start. Round 1 is open to everyone. You only need your idea, the Skill Developer Package, and your code. 🖥️ Test on real hardware for free. Each Finalist gets one assigned testing day of free remote access to a UGREEN AI NAS iDX6011 Pro. 🎨 Build what you care about. Choose from four tracks: work automation, personal memories, creative media, or your own original idea. 🤝 Connect with the UGREEN team. Access developer resources and technical support, with opportunities to win prizes, gain exposure through UGREEN, and explore future collaborations.

contests.title: Learn AR with SPECS
contests.description: Design an augmented reality app for glasses, and let an AI coding agent build it in Lens Studio. You don't need the glasses, because everything runs in Lens Studio's preview on your laptop. You'll get a short concept video, a skill pack for your coding agent, a live build session, and a live project review. $2,500 in prizes each round. ABOUT THE CHALLENGE Screens won't be the only place we use computers. Glasses are coming, and building for them is different from building for a laptop or a phone. Most first tries at AR end up as a website floating in front of your face. Good AR does things a laptop can't do: It shares your view. The camera sees what you see, so the app can respond to it. It draws in the world. Content sits on the table, over the stove, at real size, right where it belongs. It leaves your body free. Your hands stay available and your eyes stay up, so you can keep doing the real thing. Coding agents can now build a working Lens from a good description. So the hard part is deciding what's worth building and how it should feel. That's what this hackathon teaches. You'll install our Devpost Learn skill pack in your coding agent. It interviews you about your idea, checks it against AR design best practices, and writes a design brief. Then Snap's CLAD agents build the Lens in Lens Studio from that brief, and you try it in the preview. You'll finish with a working Lens, the plan behind it, and a way of thinking about AR you can use on every project after this one. WHY JOIN Learn what makes a good AR app, from the design decisions an agent can't make for you. Build for SPECS, Snap's AR glasses, without owning a pair. Try Snap's newest agent tools: CLAD, the Lens Studio MCP, and LEAF testing. Get help from real people in a live build session and a live project review. Compete to win a share of $2,500. First place takes $1,250, and every winner gets a feature in the Devpost newsletter and on Devpost's socials. Everyone who submits an eligible project gets a Devpost Learn badge and a special role in the Devpost Discord. GET STARTED You'll need a computer that runs Lens Studio, Node.js and Git, and a coding agent that supports skills. Set up your tools with the quick start on the Resources tab: your coding agent, Lens Studio, the Lens Studio MCP, and the CLAD plugin. Can't sign in to the developer platform on Lens Studio 5.24? Use Lens Studio 5.23.2 instead. Watch the concept video (at the top of this page). It's short, and it covers the design ideas the judges look for. Install the skill pack: npx skills add challengepost/learn-specs --all -y. Then open your coding agent and say "Run the plan-lens skill." It takes it from there. Join the SPECS channel in the Devpost Discord for questions and to see what other builders are making. Register for the Build for SPECS: AR Design with Lens Studio and CLAD live build session on Thursday, Oct 29 at 12PM ET. We build a Lens start to finish. It's recorded if you can't make it. Come to the SPECS Live Review: Inside the Judging Criteria on Thursday, Nov 5 at 12PM ET. We review a few projects in progress against the judging criteria, so you still have time to act on the feedback before the deadline. Want yours reviewed live? Post it in the #devpost-learn-feedback channel in the Discord and tag it "Learn AR with SPECS" and "Will It Ship." Stuck? Ask in the Discord channel. Setup help, the FAQ, and event details are on the Resources tab.

contests.title: QNX Global Hackathon
contests.description: For decades, QNX has been running the systems people bet their lives on, from medical devices and factory floors to trains, robots, and more than 275 million vehicles. It guarantees not just that your code runs, but exactly when. Now QNX 8.0 is free for non-commercial use, and the QNX team wants to see what you do with it when nobody hands you a spec. Build a robot that reacts in microseconds instead of milliseconds. Write the driver nobody has written yet. Port something you love to QNX, or build the tooling you always wished existed. If it runs on QNX 8.0, or helps someone else build for it, it counts. Pick your category and compete for a share of $50,000. Show us what you can do! Why join? Get your hands on a real-time OS, free. QNX Everywhere gives you QNX SDP 8.0, QNX Developer Desktop, and the QNX Hypervisor for non-commercial use, plus free training courses to get you moving. No target hardware required; QEMU works, and so does a Raspberry Pi 5. In 275 million vehicles. Now on your laptop. Not a teaching edition or a stripped-down trial. It's the same QNX that ships in commercial systems, and until QNX Everywhere, building on it meant a commercial license. Compete for $50,000 in prizes. Plus swag, a coffee chat with a QNX exec, and a feature on the QNX blog and social channels. Get Started Get free access to QNX SDP 8.0 through QNX Everywhere (5 minutes) Run through the QNX SDP 8.0 Quick Start Guide and get a program running on your target or QEMU (45 minutes) Browse QNX sample projects and open-source ports, then pick your category (30 minutes)

contests.title: DSH Hacks V2 ($100k+ in prizes!)
contests.description: DSH Hacks V2 is a global student competition open to students aged 13+ hosted collaboratively by three youth-led organizations: DeltaForge Hacks, NXT Horizon, and STEMise. Theme: AI x Healthcare This event brings together young innovators from around the world to transform bold ideas into technical products that address the health challenges facing our world today. Participants will work individually or in teams to identify a real-world healthcare problem and design and develop a meaningful technical solution. Projects may range from diagnostic tools tackling global disease burdens, to patient-care platforms improving access and outcomes, to AI-powered systems reimagining how we detect, treat, and manage illness. Creativity, feasibility, technical depth, clinical insight, and real-world impact will be central to evaluation. The theme of this competition is to build technical solutions that solve pressing healthcare problems. These solutions can be an app, a website, a simulation, a system, or an algorithm. Participants are encouraged to use AI to help them build a meaningful solution and to lower the technical barrier that poses challenges for beginners with ambitious project ideas.

contests.title: Arbiter Hacks V1
contests.description: About the challenge Arbiter Hacks V1 runs two parallel tracks. Pick one when you register, or switch before the submission deadline. You may only submit to one track. General Track: Build anything. Any language, any stack, any idea. This track rewards technical ambition and execution, regardless of subject. Theme Track, Rethinking Waste: Build something that helps people or systems reduce, sort, or recycle waste more effectively. Examples include a tool that identifies whether an item is recyclable, an app that routes food waste to donation, a hardware or vision system that sorts materials, or a dataset or model that improves recycling accuracy. If it moves the needle on waste, it fits. The tracks are judged separately, against separate rubrics, for separate prizes. A polished General submission and a high-impact Theme submission compete only within their own track. Get started Register and pick a track. Form a team of [1 to 4] or go solo. Late submissions are not judged.

contests.title: AWS MSP AI Hackathon
contests.description: What would your MSP look like if AI handled the alerts, predicted the capacity crunch, and powered a whole new line of customer services? The AWS MSP AI Hackathon is your chance to build it, and to show AWS and the partner community what an AI-first MSP looks like in practice. Build production-ready AI solutions with AWS AI Services such as: Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents, Amazon Quick, Kiro, the AWS Frontier Agents, etc. (See the full list on the FAQs) Use AI to run your MSP better, or to deliver new AI-driven services your customers can’t get anywhere else. We’re not looking for proofs of concept. We want real solutions that deliver measurable impact and scale across MSP environments. Why You Should Participate Build What’s Next for Your MSP: Get hands-on with AWS’s latest agentic AI services and turn them into solutions your team and customers can use. Solve Real Problems: Tackle the challenges MSPs face every day, from incident response and FinOps to customer-facing AI services. Win Big: Compete for $64,000 in cash prizes across two tracks and 10 Special Prizes. Get Your Solution in Front of AWS: Track winners earn a spot in the MSP AI Use Case Library, priority consideration for AWS go-to-market support, and white-glove enablement for a potential AWS Marketplace listing. Get Recognized: Standout solutions may be highlighted at the AWS Global Partner Summit. Get started Confirm Your Eligibility: Make sure your organization is an MSP partner or part of the AWS Partner Network. (Click here for full eligibility requirements) Register and Join the Community: Sign up on Devpost and join the hackathon Discord to connect with AWS experts and other partners. Claim Your Credits: Request $200 in AWS credits for your AWS account. One set of credits per AWS Account ID. Credits are available while supplies last. Click here to apply. Pick Your Track: Review the examples on the Resources page, choose Track 1 or Track 2, and start building!
